“Breastfeeding causes tooth decay.” That was the headline making the rounds.

But here’s what the study actually involved: rats without salivary glands were given sugar water, soda, milk, and breast milk. Soda badly damaged their teeth; breast milk had little effect. Guess which one got the alarming headline? Breastfeeding. And who funded the study? Abbott Laboratories—a formula company.

That’s why headlines deserve a closer look. Breastfeeding isn’t what’s ruining your child’s teeth. Poor airway development can lead to mouth breathing, which dries out saliva—the mouth’s natural defense against cavities.

The Palace Survives Its Staff

Yemen’s prime minister and Cabinet survived the Houthi attack on their presidential compound. Five people working there did not.

Missiles and drones struck Aden’s al-Maashiq Palace on Oct. 15, killing five people and injuring 16, according to Yemen’s health minister. The casualties included guards and civilian employees. Prime Minister Shaya al-Zindani and his ministers were unharmed.

The Houthis said they targeted a Saudi military operations center. An unnamed Yemeni minister told AFP that missiles hit command centers used by government and Saudi-led coalition forces inside the compound. 

Zindani condemned the attack as another example of Houthi strikes on civilian sites. The palace apparently changes categories depending on who is describing it.

Meanwhile, the Saudi-led coalition says Houthi attacks on Riyadh’s airport have killed 17 people and injured 333 this month. 

The Houthis had warned airlines and workers to leave Saudi airports and oil facilities.

⚡️ Economy minister urges faster resolution of IsDB-backed projects

📌 Tehran, IRNA — Minister of Economic Affairs and Finance Ali Madanizadeh has stressed expediting the resolution of approved projects, removing executive obstacles, and utilizing the financing capacities of the Islamic Development Bank to complete the country’s priority projects.

Speaking in a meeting with Muhammad Sulaiman Al Jasser, President of the Islamic Development Bank (IsDB), which was held on the sidelines of the Annual Meetings of the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank Group in Bangkok on Friday, Madanizadeh said he had exchanged views on the implementation of projects supported by this bank and ways to strengthen financial and developmental cooperation.
​
Following up on approved projects and removing obstacles to their implementation, especially in the environmental, urban wastewater, and educational infrastructure development sectors, were among the main issues discussed, he added.
​
Extending the validity and re-approval of certain priority projects whose evaluation stages had previously been completed were on the agenda of the meetings, he noted.
​
Both sides emphasized pursuing the use of remaining allocated credits to complete projects currently underway, he stated.
​
Strengthening banking coordination, resolving payments related to installments, and facilitating the repayment process of financial obligations were among the other topics raised in this meeting, Madanizadeh said.
​
The meeting underscored the importance of continuing technical consultations, clearing existing hurdles, and concentrating efforts on finishing incomplete projects, intending to leverage cooperation opportunities with the IsDB more efficiently.
